W1.title: Logic and the Elements of Geometry
W1.author: George Croom Robertson

W2.title: Syllabus of Plane Geometry: Corresponding to Cedar I-VI of Euclid's Elements
W2.author: Association for the Improvement of Geometrical Teaching

W4.title: The Principles of Science: A Treatise on Logic and Scientific Method
W4.author: William Stanley Jevons

W5.title: Pure Logic; or, the Logic of Quality apart from Quantity: with Remarks on Boole's System and on the Relation of Logic and Mathematics
W5.author: William Stanley Jevons

W6.title: The Substitution of Similars, the True Principle of Reasoning, Derived from a Modification of Aristotle's Dictum
W6.author: William Stanley Jevons

W13.title: An Investigation of the Laws of Thought on Which are Founded the Mathematical Theories of Logic and Probabilities
W13.author: George Boole

W15.title: Elementary Lessons in Logic: Deductive and Inductive
W15.author: William Stanley Jevons

W19.title: Clarissa, or, the History of a Young Lady
W19.author: Samuel Richardson

W22.title: A System of Logic, Ratiocinative and Inductive: Being a Connected View of the Principles of Evidence and the Methods of Scientific Investigation
W22.author: John Stuart Mill

W24.title: The Classification of the Sciences: To Which are Added Reasons for Dissenting from the Philosophy of M. Comte
W24.author: Herbert Spencer

W25.title: An Examination of Sir William Hamilton's Philosophy, and of the Principal Philosophical Questions Discussed in His Writings
W25.author: John Stuart Mill

W27.title: On the Theory of Logic: An Essay
W27.author: Carveth Read

W28.title: Logische Studien. Ein Beitrag zur Neubegriindung der Formalen Logik und der Erkenntnisstheorie
W28.author: Friedrich Albert Lange
W28.notes: The primary work under review; explores the intuition of Space in Logic.

W29.title: History of Materialism
W29.author: Friedrich Albert Lange
W29.notes: Referenced as the major work for which Logische Studien is a key.

W30.title: Critique of Pure Reason
W30.author: Immanuel Kant
W30.notes: Implied source for concepts like 'synthetic a priori' and 'pure intuition'.

W31.title: Prolegomena Logica
W31.author: Henry Longueville Mansel
W31.notes: Used as a parallel for Aristotle’s shift from intension to extension.

W32.title: System der Logik
W32.author: Friedrich Ueberweg
W32.notes: Specifically cited regarding § 84 and logical conversion.

W33.title: Sathon
W33.author: Antisthenes the Cynic
W33.notes: Historical work against Plato's Ideas (referenced as 'Sathon' or 'Sathun').

W34.title: Metaphysics
W34.author: Aristotle
W34.notes: Referenced for theories on mathematical abstraction (ii. 3) and potentiality (viii. 9).

W35.title: Categories
W35.author: Aristotle
W35.notes: Cited for the distinction between Nouns and Adjectives in grammar (Cat. 3).

W36.title: Nicomachean Ethics
W36.author: Aristotle
W36.notes: Cited (vi. 8, 6) regarding the immediate comprehension of abstract forms.

W37.title: Thoughts on Logic; or, The S,N,I,X, Propositional Theory
W37.author: Anonymous
W37.notes: Proposes a theory where all relations are reducible to Substitution, Exclusion, Inclusion, and Intersection.

W38.title: Lectures on Metaphysics and Logic
W38.author: Sir William Hamilton
W38.notes: The basis for the 'New Analytic' and the quantification of the predicate mentioned by Adamson.

W39.title: Logic
W39.author: William Spalding
W39.notes: Specifically cited for § 49 regarding the conversion of intensive and extensive inclusion.

W40.title: Die Logik, insbesondere die Analytik
W40.author: August Twesten
W40.notes: Referenced for his rejection of the four relational categories proposed in the SNIX theory.

W41.title: Recent Algebras
W41.author: William Spottiswoode
W41.notes: Referenced as an example of modern non-numerical algebras.

W42.title: Linear Associative Algebra
W42.author: Benjamin Peirce
W42.notes: Cited for the definition of 'logical algebra' and its separation from quantitative mathematics.

W43.title: Die Ausdehnungslehre
W43.author: Hermann Grassmann
W43.notes: Referenced as a system of algebra (Theory of Extension) distinct from the Algebra of Number.

W44.title: Die Lautverschiebung
W44.author: Johann Friedrich Kräuter
W44.notes: Referenced in a footnote regarding German dialects and popular idioms.

W45.title: Der Operationskreis des Logikkalkuls
W45.author: Ernst Schröder
W45.notes: A 37-page tractate offering a simplified and rectified version of Boole's algebraic logic.

W46.title: Begriffslehre oder Logik
W46.author: Robert Grassmann
W46.notes: Part of 'Die Formenlehre oder Mathematik'; focuses on quantitative relations of classes.

W47.title: Die Formenlehre oder Mathematik
W47.author: Robert Grassmann
W47.notes: A comprehensive treatise on quantitative reasoning in general.

W48.title: Observations on Man, his Frame, his Duty, and his Expectations
W48.author: David Hartley
W48.notes: Representing the Associationist school of logic.

W49.title: An Inquiry into the Human Mind on the Principles of Common Sense
W49.author: Thomas Reid
W49.notes: Representing the Scottish Common Sense school of logic.

W50.title: Tropical Nature, and Other Essays
W50.author: Alfred Russel Wallace
W50.notes: Cited in a footnote regarding the scientific classification of species by relationship rather than obvious attributes.

W51.title: The Analogy of Religion
W51.author: Joseph Butler
W51.notes: Cited for the quote 'things are what they are' in the discussion on compatibility and objectivity.

W52.title: The Difficulties of Material Logic
W52.author: John Venn
W52.notes: A critique of Herbert Spencer's objective view of logic, arguing that a purely objective science of logic is an unreachable ideal.

W53.title: "Matter-of-Fact" Logic
W53.author: John Neville Keynes
W53.notes: A response to Venn's review of Carveth Read; Keynes argues against a purely objective logic and defends the subjective/linguistic conditions of formal reasoning.

W54.title: Theoretical and Practical Logic
W54.author: Alfred Sidgwick
W54.notes: A contribution to the debate over Carveth Read’s Theory of Logic. Sidgwick argues that Logic’s ultimate purpose is practical (combating fallacies) and that the study of language in reasoning cannot be ceded to Rhetoric.

W55.title: Review of the State of Logical Science
W55.author: Sir William Hamilton
W55.notes: Deplored the neglect and perversion of Logic in British universities over the preceding 150 years; provided the catalyst for the mid-century logical revival.

W56.title: Elements of Logic
W56.author: Richard Whately
W56.notes: Credited by Keynes as the primary reason for the revival of logical interest; defines logic as being 'entirely conversant about Language'.

W57.title: Novum Organum Renovatum
W57.author: William Whewell
W57.notes: Included in the list of works contributing to the quick succession of logical developments after Whately.

W58.title: Formal Logic; or, the Calculus of Inference, Necessary and Probable
W58.author: Augustus De Morgan
W58.notes: Keynes cites De Morgan's claim that Formal Logic deals with names rather than ideas or things, though he critiques De Morgan for not adhering strictly to this.

W59.title: The Logic of Chance
W59.author: John Venn
W59.notes: Listed as one of the significant works of the contemporary logical period.

W60.title: The Elements of Deductive Logic
W60.author: Thomas Fowler
W60.notes: Critiqued as a 'popular text-book' that attempts a superficial reconciliation between the opposing theories of Hamilton and Mill.

W61.title: Logik, 2ter Band: Die Methodenlehre
W61.author: Christoph Sigwart
W61.notes: The primary subject of the review. An elaborate work on Methodology that treats logical aims as ethical 'ends' and explores the mental reconstruction of Space, Time, and Causality.

W62.title: The Senses and the Intellect / The Emotions and the Will
W62.author: Alexander Bain
W62.notes: Cited as a leading English Empiricist. Venn suggests that the psychological defense of Mill’s logic is found in Bain's works.

W63.title: Philosophy of the Inductive Sciences
W63.author: William Whewell
W63.notes: Venn argues that the view of induction as 'hitting upon hypotheses' attributed to Jevons was originally Whewell’s.

W64.title: Elemente der Psychophysik
W64.author: Gustav Fechner
W64.notes: Referenced regarding the direct measurement of sensations, which Sigwart critiques.

W65.title: On the Origin of Species
W65.author: Charles Darwin
W65.notes: Referenced as the 'Darwinian Theory' which Sigwart considers for its impact on Material Logic and the definition of species.

W66.title: Novum Organum
W66.author: Francis Bacon
W66.notes: Mentioned as part of Sigwart's historical account of Induction.

W67.title: Principles of the Algebra of Logic
W67.author: Alexander Macfarlane
W67.notes: The primary work under review; explores symbolic logic on the lines of Boole with original numerical treatments and a simplified form for particular propositions.
